content_units: A low-cost, phone-free evening that balances movement, watching, teamwork, and a calm finish. This plan is built for   14 students aged 13–15   with mixed attention spans and avoids horror content.
Time   Activity   Format   Why it works   Materials
18:00-18:15   Common Ground Sprint   Icebreaker   Fast, active, low-pressure, gets everyone talking without putting one teen on the spot   Open space; optional chairs
18:15-19:00   Short-form screening block   Watch + react   Better for mixed attention spans than a full movie; easy to pause between clips   Projector/TV, speakers
19:00-19:10   Snack/stretch reset   Break   Prevents energy drop and restlessness   Water/snacks if available
19:10-19:50   Team Challenge: Marshmallow Tower Remix   Collaborative game   Strong teamwork, funny, creative, and very low cost   Spaghetti, tape, string, paper, marshmallow or paper ball
19:50-20:15   Mini Awards + Vote Wall   Closing group activity   Reflective but still playful; lets quieter students contribute   Sticky notes, pens, wall/board
20:15-20:30   Pack-down + informal exit chat   Wind-down   Smooth finish and supervised transition to pickup/home time   Music optional, chairs
- Ask everyone to stand in a circle.
- “Move to this side if you like sweet snacks.”
- “Move to this side if you’d rather watch comedy than action.”
- “Step in if you’ve ever built something from LEGO.”
- Keep it quick:   10-12 prompts   over 15 minutes.
- easy for late arrivals to join
Use a   40-45 minute block   instead of one full film. This is the best match for mixed attention spans.
- 18:45-19:00: 1 final short or selected episode segment
- a single episode of a family-friendly sitcom or CBBC-style program
- avoid horror, intense suspense, and romance-heavy picks
- choose content with clear visual storytelling and light humor
- use subtitles if your room audio is uneven
- official YouTube channels for family-friendly animated shorts, only if pre-screened and ad-managed safely
- Build the tallest free-standing tower in   18 minutes
- Must support a marshmallow on top
- If food is awkward, use a paper ball instead
Add a remix twist for teens:
- round 2: facilitator announces one rule change, such as:
- funny and energetic without being chaotic
- gives natural roles to different personalities
Closing Activity: Vote Wall + Mini Awards
Then do   mini awards   for 10 minutes:
- each student says   one word   for the night, or passes
This closes the session positively without forcing deep sharing.
- Chairs in a semicircle for screening
- 3 tables or floor zones for team game
-   £8-£20   depending on snacks and what you already have
- avoid jump scares, heavy themes, or crude humor
- keep total passive watching under   45 minutes
- have one backup non-screen game ready in case tech fails
If you want the safest, easiest version to run, use this exact sequence:
This is the strongest option because it is   cheap, structured, lively, and flexible   if energy levels shift.
